findings.title: Keep GraphQLError's no-stack fallback under test
findings.trigger: The test `creates new stack if original error has no stack` now passes `new Error('original')`, which has a `stack`, so GraphQLError copies that stack through its first branch (src/error/GraphQLError.js:195-200) and the `Error.captureStackTrace` fallback (lines 201-209) runs in no test.
findings.impact: At the merge-base `{ message: 'original' }` exercised the fallback; at the head `expect(e.stack).to.be.a('string')` observes the copied stack, which the preceding test already covers, so a regression that leaves `stack` undefined when `originalError` has none would pass silently. The change description records no decision to drop this protection.
findings.change: Give `original` a stackless value that still type-checks, for example `const original: any = { message: 'original' };` (the `any` pattern src/error/__tests__/locatedError-test.js:29 already uses), or delete `stack` from the constructed Error before passing it.
findings.source: Rubric, Changed tests: an existing test that could catch its defect at the merge-base but no longer can at head.

observations.fact: Only the `declare class` constructor signature gained `| null` for `nodes`; the implementation function's own `nodes` annotation still reads `$ReadOnlyArray<ASTNode> | ASTNode | void`, while the body already treats `null` as no nodes.
